clue.text: "Golden Ass" diary is kept by passionate guy with interest in 7 and 21, and parts of 2, 4, 6, 8, 13, 17, 23, 24 and 26

definitions.text: guy with interest in 7 and 21, and parts of 2, 4, 6, 8, 13, 17, 23, 24 and 26

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold, so golden gives OR
an ass is a fool, and a nit is a fool too

indicators.note: something kept by another is held inside it, so these letters go inside the next piece

parts.note: passionate means hot
a log is a daily record, like a diary
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lusty man keeps a journal about The Golden Ass and has a curious set of hobbies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is kept by' marks the container. The definition is the long tail: 7 and 21 are birds outright, and each other listed answer holds a bird (ROBIN, HEN, GOOSE, DUCK, TIT, TEAL, COCK, SWALLOW).
explanation.definitionFit: A bird expert studies swifts, macaws and every other species hidden in the listed entries.

clue.text: Dressin' gown's partner was outlawed

definitions.note: the clue reads as a sentence about the figure who was outlawed, so the definition is the person described

parts.note: dressing is robing, and the dropped g of Dressin' drops the G of robing
an academic gown is worn with a hood

explanation.surface: Someone's dressing gown went with a partner who was banished.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Dressin'' is the signal: ROBING loses its G. The outlaw of Sherwood Forest is the English folk hero who robbed the rich.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary archer of Sherwood was declared an outlaw and lived beyond the law with his band.

clue.text: The baby is a girl

parts.note: taken as written
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A parent announces that the new baby is a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, so a baby is someone's issue.

clue.text: Mrs Shakespeare opening up plant

indicators.note: in a down entry, up says the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Shakespeare's wife was Anne Hathaway; her first name plus the opening letter of her surname gives these letters

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's wife digs up a plant in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ANNEH, Anne plus the H opening Hathaway, to give the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a shrub whose leaves give a reddish dye for hair and skin.

clue.text: A long way from a girl they produced

indicators.note: produced suggests the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A distant place, far from where they brought up a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges the nine letters of 'a girl they'.
explanation.definitionFit: A light year is the distance light travels in a year, an enormous span.

clue.text: Leave work without much money in Rome and don't bend the knee

parts.note: to leave is to go

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the work wraps round the money

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: much of the money, not all of it, so the coin's name is cut short

parts.note: the sesterce was an ancient Roman coin

explanation.surface: Someone quits a job while broke in Italy and refuses to kneel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much' keeps most of the coin's name, SESTE, and 'without' (old sense: outside) wraps the work round it. Soldiers on parade march with straight legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The stiff-legged military march swings each leg out without bending at the knee.

clue.text: Satirist's riddle about Whitehead

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so Satirist's reads as the satirist is

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve, so to riddle is to sift
the head, or first letter, of White

explanation.surface: A satirist poses a puzzle concerning someone called Whitehead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riddle' looks like a puzzle but is the sieve; Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels. The answer is also a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift was the Anglo-Irish author of satires such as A Modest Proposal.

clue.text: Provider of cricketing scene, 0-1-0, provokes old-fashioned exclamation

parts.note: Thomas Lord founded Lord's, the London cricket ground
nought is love in tennis, one is a, and nought is a duck in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket score line of nought, one, nought makes someone exclaim in an old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's in north London is the home of English cricket, named after Thomas Lord. A duck is a batsman's score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated cry of surprise, the sort of thing a Cockney might say in an old film.

clue.text: Shan't play with cosy arrangement — mind my own business

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to play along with a snug set-up and tells others to keep out of their affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges SHANT, PLAY and COSY; 'with' only joins them. The definition reads as a brush-off but means minds are this person's trade.
explanation.definitionFit: This therapist's work is the mind, so the mind is literally their own business.

clue.text: American singer or ruminant

parts.note: taken as written
the bison is a cud-chewing animal

explanation.surface: Was that an American vocalist or a grazing beast?
explanation.walkthrough: Roy Orbison was the American singer of Oh, Pretty Woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Roy Orbison was a famous American rock and roll vocalist.

clue.text: Splendid achievements in learning keeping one in grammar school

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the school's abbreviation
keeping means holding inside, so one goes inside learning

parts.note: lore is learning or knowledge
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fine accomplishments in study at a selective school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' and 'in' are nested containers. A British grammar school is a selective state secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: Glories are triumphs or magnificent deeds worthy of praise.

clue.text: A fool to try to get money from church

parts.words: to try to get money from
parts.note: to dun someone is to press them for payment of a debt
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Only an idiot would ask the church for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow-witted person, a dullard.

clue.text: Genuine class article needed in opposing Conservative

indicators.note: these pieces are required inside the next one

parts.note: anti means opposing
U is upper class, as in U and non-U
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A real classy piece is wanted by a Tory who is against things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed in' splits the opposing word after its A; class is U, as in the old U and non-U distinction of upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic means real, not fake or copied.

clue.text: Providers of music for 'omeless vagrants

indicators.note: the dropped H of 'omeless shows the H is dropped from the word it describes

parts.note: hoboes are tramps or vagrants

explanation.surface: Buskers play tunes for down-and-outs.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''omeless' is the signal: the H is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboes are woodwind instruments that produce music.

clue.text: Street by a river at end of flight?

parts.note: taken as written
the Irwell is a river through Manchester and Salford

explanation.surface: A road beside a river where an air journey finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests aircraft, but it is a flight of stairs. The IRWELL is a river in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A stairwell is the shaft holding a staircase, where each flight of steps begins and ends.

clue.text: Number playing football here is 8

definitions.meaning: two teams of eleven make the count of players on the pitch
in this puzzle, entry 22 is the word for 8

explanation.surface: A football team count, and a reference within the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 22-down in this very grid is EIGHT, so 'here' 22 is 8.
explanation.definitionFit: Two sides of eleven put twenty-two players on a football pitch.

clue.text: Time for old rebel to go in ferry to restaurant

indicators.note: to go in means to be placed inside

parts.note: a ro-ro is a roll-on roll-off ferry
Jack Cade led a rebellion in England in 1450

explanation.surface: A period of time while an old insurgent boards a ferry to dine out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go in' marks the container. Jack Cade led the Kentish revolt of 1450; the Trocadero was a famous London restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trocadero was a well-known restaurant and entertainment venue off Piccadilly Circus.

clue.text: Othello, say, drunk, will sway, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: tight means drunk, and tight'll roll is a drunk who will sway

explanation.surface: Othello, for instance, staggers about drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'tight'll roll' gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the leading part named in the play's title.

clue.text: Reschedule an overdue attempt

indicators.note: to reschedule is to rearrange, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A late task gets moved to another date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reschedule' rearranges AN OVERDUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an earnest try or effort.

clue.text: Russian scrum half's job?

definitions.meaning: a Russian, here the Russian president
in rugby the scrum half feeds the ball into the scrum

explanation.surface: A Russian is joked about as a rugby player.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union, the scrum half rolls the ball into the scrum: that act is the put-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Putin is the Russian president; put-in is the scrum half's feed.

clue.text: Draw a line at entering diplomatic move without aspiration

indicators.note: entering means going inside the following piece
aspiration is the breathy H sound, so H is dropped

parts.note: a demarche is a diplomatic step or protest
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diplomat makes a move, drawing a line in the sand without ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without aspiration' drops the breathed H, leaving DEMARCE, and 'entering' marks the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To demarcate is to mark out a boundary or limit.

clue.text: Bird (hen) to sound like another

parts.note: a mother hen, so hen gives ma, mother
a caw is the call of another bird, the crow

explanation.surface: A hen tries to imitate another bird's call.
explanation.walkthrough: Mother hen cawing like a crow gives the parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large, brightly coloured parrot.

clue.text: Pieces in a row?

parts.note: a row of a chessboard holds this many pieces at the start, and a rowing crew has this many oars

explanation.definitionFit: A chessboard row has this many squares, so a full back rank holds this many chessmen.

clue.text: Take a little, waste a lot

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pinch a small amount, or squander plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal is to take something without permission.

clue.text: Conductor of notes

parts.note: sol is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A conductor known for notes.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Georg Solti was a Hungarian-born conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Solti was a celebrated orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Squint shows salmon with new leader

indicators.note: the first letter is replaced by a different one

parts.note: the sockeye is a Pacific salmon

explanation.surface: A fish shown with a fresh head looks cross-eyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with new leader' swaps the S of SOCKEYE for C.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockeye is an eye that squints or turns.

clue.text: God gives green light for capital punishment?

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for God
giving the green light is allowing something

explanation.surface: The deity permits the death penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: the gallows is a means of capital punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The gallows is the frame used to hang people, a form of execution.

clue.text: Entertaining follower, ate like a kite

indicators.note: entertaining in the sense of holding, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: to swallow food is to eat it
a tail is someone who follows another

explanation.surface: A diner entertains a guest, eating like a bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining' marks the container. Kite is the forked-tailed bird of prey, not the toy on a string.
explanation.definitionFit: Kites have deeply forked tails like a swallow's.
